name: Blue box
died_because: Inter-office trunks migrated to CCIS (No.6) then SS7, moving supervision out-of-band. A properly conditioned blue-box call was already impractical on major US routes by 1990.

name: Red box
power_source: battery; canonically a Radio Shack tone dialer (43-141 / 43-146) with the 3.579545 MHz crystal replaced by a 6.5536 MHz crystal (ratio ~1.831, retuning '*' to ~1723+2213 Hz, inside ACTS ±1.5% tolerance)
died_because: ACTS-equipped Bell single-slot payphones were retrofitted/replaced by locally-validating smart phones (Millennium/COCOT) 1996-2002; COCOTs never had the vuln. Largely inert in North America by 2002.

name: Black box
power_source: DC circuit across the called loop (resistor/capacitor)
died_because: Prevented answer supervision from returning to the originating CO so the caller wasn't billed. Dead once answer supervision moved out-of-band (CCIS/SS7 ANM); keeping the local loop off-hook no longer matters.

name: Green box
died_because: Spoofed TSPS operator coin-control tones from the caller side. Only worked in specific four-wire topologies with poor filtering; obsolete with digital operator systems.

name: Beige box
died_because: Not a signaling attack — a butt set with alligator clips for subscriber-line access at a B-box or NID. Still works on any twisted-pair POTS drop.

name: Aqua box
died_because: Claimed to defeat an FBI 'line lock' hold by draining voltage. Technical validity disputed; recorded as folklore.

disputed.validity: Community-reported only; no credible primary confirmation the mechanism worked.
